meaning: something that is very easy to do
example: My oral exam was a piece of cake after weeks of practice.
origin: Its exact origin is uncertain. It is thought to come from early twentieth-century American slang

wrong_meanings.meaning: a dessert served at the end of a meal
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal meaning, not the idiomatic one. The idiom has nothing to do with food.

wrong_meanings.meaning: a sweet reward given to students after class
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom does not refer to rewards or treats. It describes how easy a task is.

wrong_meanings.meaning: a difficult task that takes a long time
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom. A piece of cake is something that is simple and quick.

explanation: 'A piece of cake' means that a task is very easy. It is used informally when something turns out to require little effort, for example an exam or a presentation you have prepared well.
